evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學
evidence.field: 形義通解；《說文》與《廣韻》資料
evidence.text: The entry for 叚 reports bronze forms analyzed as 爪 + 又 with 石 as phonetic (the mouth portion of 石 simplified to two short strokes). It records Xu Shen’s gloss 借也, “borrow,” and cites bronze uses read as 嘏 “blessing,” 瑕 “fault,” and 胡/何 “what/why”; it gives 廣韻 古疋切. This supports a graphic and phonetic account for 叚, but the bronze-form description is the source’s analysis, not a visually inspected glyph in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 田炜, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心 article reprinted by Sohu
evidence.text: The author reports that pre-Qin excavated texts contain 叚 but not 假, and that 假 first appears in Qin-period documents. He discusses a dated Liye document from Qin Shihuang year 26 (221 BCE): in the author’s reading, 叚 marks lending/giving out while 假 marks borrowing/obtaining. He proposes 假 was formed by adding semantic 人 to 叚 to distinguish a use of the word, while noting that Shuowen and Duan Yucai explain the relationship differently and do not explicitly explain why 人 marks “false.” This is a scholarly proposal, not an uncontested account of character formation.
evidence.title: 〖学闻〗田炜：说“叚”“假”

evidence.source: 田炜, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心 article reprinted by Sohu
evidence.text: The article quotes Shuowen’s analysis of 假 as 从人叚声, “非真也,” and reports Duan Yucai’s view that 假 and 叚 are near-identical in meaning. The author disputes a simple account in which “false” is derived from “borrow,” proposing a graphic differentiation of the written forms instead. The article also notes that later texts no longer consistently maintain the Qin-period 叚/假 distinction; a Han silk manuscript uses 假 for both borrowing and lending. These points separate graphic differentiation from a proposed semantic history.
evidence.title: 〖学闻〗田炜：说“叚”“假”

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, 香港中文大學

It does not date each cited inscription on the viewed page. The bronzes establish older graph uses for readings other than 假’s “false” sense, but do not by themselves prove the chronology of semantic development for 假.
